previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and long-standing substance use was admitted for acute shortness of breath following five days of medication non-compliance, high salt intake, and crack cocaine use. He reported increased depression and passive suicidal ideation preceding substance use. On admission, he was tachycardic and hypoxemic with bibasilar crackles and a low room air oxygen saturation. Imaging showed chronic interstitial lung disease with possible acute exacerbation. He was diagnosed with chemical pneumonitis superimposed on underlying lung disease, managed with a short course of steroids, bronchodilators, and insulin titration for hyperglycemia. His condition improved with treatment, tachycardia resolved, and oxygenation stabilized. He was discharged to an extended care facility for ongoing medical and psychiatric support, with plans to restart losartan and torsemide after renal function follow-up and to continue close monitoring of blood glucose, weight, and mental health.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ y/o male with a history of non-ischemic 
cardiomyopathy (LVEF 20%), COPD, HTN, HLD, IDDM, schizophrenia 
and polysubstance abuse who presented with shortness of breath

# Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis: Evaluated by pulmonology, 
elicited recent h/o smoking crack cocaine prior to this 
admission. In light of this, symptoms and CT changes thought to 
represent hypersensitivity pnueumonitis. His initial O2 
requirement trended down to 50% FiO2 by facemask, with multiple 
triggers for hypoxia that was treated with IV lasix to no 
effect. He remained on the floor, gradually tolerating nasal 
canula by HD 5. He was started on 60mg prednisone daily for 7 
days, ending ___, and then 12 day taper ending ___. His 
symptoms rapidly improved to where he was saturating 95% on room 
air by HD 7. Patient scheduled for pulmonology followup.

# PNA?: Febrile on admission, leukocytosis with fevers overnight 
HD2 on Vanc/Cefepime/Azithro for HCAP. Blood and urine cultures 
negative, urine legionella negative, flu A and B negative, 
fungal studies pending at time of discharge. CXR and CTA were 
c/w multifocal PNA vs. chemical alveolitis, possibly infection 
overlying baseline disease. Oxygen saturation remained poor. 
Patient completed 8 day course of vanc/cefepime/azithromycin and 
was discharged afebrile x6 days, no leukocytosis, and negative 
growth on blood cultures and urine cultures. 

# ___: Likely prerenal due to excessive diuresis in an effort to 
treat perceived fluid overload, Cr peaked at 2.9 with oliguria, 
resolved with gentle IVF, eventually diuresed effectively on 
reduced dose of torsemide 30mg instead of prior home dose of 
40mg.

# Chronic Systolic Heart Failure: Patient has a baseline EF of 
20%, considering exacerbation possibly triggered by HCAP vs. 
crack inhalation. This is in the setting of not taking his 
medications, primarily his diuretic, for 3 days. Echo unchanged 
from prior - EF still 20%. Patient diuresed HD 1 and 2 with 40IV 
lasix x4, urine output initially 600cc, decreased with rising Cr 
and inconsistent evidence of vol overload on exam. Determined to 
be intravasc depleted and diuresis held ___, developed ___ and 
oliguria that resolved ___. He was restarted on home torsemide 
at reduced dose of 30mg daily and digoxin 0.125mg daily once ___ 
resolved. Admission weight 85kg, discharge weight 91.2kg. 

# Tachycardia: Rates initially in the 120's, PE ruled out with 
CTA, metoprolol held in the context of possible recent cocaine 
abuse, HR trended to low 100's, metoprolol briefly restarted 
___ but discontinued at discharge with concern for overlap 
with cocaine abuse. The patient will require outpatient followup 
for rate control.

# Substance Abuse: Patient was seen by social work. He stated 
that he recognized the dangers he was putting himself in with 
his habits. 

# COPD: Continued albuterol, advair, tiotropium, in 
ipratriopium. Scheduled for PFT evaluation.

# IDDM: His last A1c was 7.7 on ___. During his last 
hospitalization there was some difficultly controlling his 
sugars. Sugars stable this admit with home Lantus and HISS.

# Anemia: Patient has microcytic anemia, previously on Fe 
supplement, discharged with additional vitamin C.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with history of crack cocaine inhalation, now
presenting with worsening hypoxemia and tachycardia.

COMPARISON:  Multiple chest radiographic examinations dating back to ___ and chest CTs from ___, ___,
___, and ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images from the thoracic inlet to the upper
abdomen were displayed with 1.25- and 5-mm slice thickness.  Intravenous
contrast was administered and arterial phase imaging was acquired.  Coronal,
sagittal, and oblique maximum intensity projection reformations were created.

CT CHEST WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:

LUNGS AND AIRWAYS:  Superimposed on a background of interstitial fibrotic
changes are confluent consolidations involving both upper lobes, right middle
lobe, lingula, and lower lobes.  As compared to multiple prior examinations,
findings are most similar to prior examination from ___. 
Intervening chest CTs, particularly the examination from ___, have
shown partial interval resolution of the superimposed confluent opacities. 
The waxing and waning confluent consolidations suggest an acute process
superimposed upon chronic infiltrative lung disease.  The imaging appearance
is most suggestive of either acute alveolar damage secondary to direct toxic
or allergic effects inhaled substance, with or without diffuse alveolar
hemorrhage.  Other alternatives in this patient population include
cocaine-induced eosinophilic lung disease.  The slightly increased bilateral
non-hemorrhagic pleural effusions, cardiac enlargement and known
cardiomyopathy, suggest some component of the lung parenchymal abnormalities
may also be due to pulmonary edema.  Infectious etiologies cannot be entirely
excluded and should be correlated with clinical signs and symptoms.  

A solitary, irregular,7 x 13 mm, spiculated nodule in the right upper lobe, is
unchanged since ___.  Aside from aerated secretions in the left mid
trachea, the tracheobronchial tree is patent to subsegmental levels, without
bronchial wall thickening or bronchiectasis.

MEDIASTINUM:  The thyroid gland is homogeneous without incidental nodule. 
Bulky mediastinal lymphadenopathy is longstanding and stable since at least
___, including a right paratracheal lymph node conglomerat, 19 mm
across, previously 18 mm (2:25).  A large subcarinal lymph node is 28 mm wide
now, 26 mm previously (2:48).  The thoracic aorta is normal.  There is no
pulmonary embolism to subsegmental levels.  Moderate biventricular 
enlargement and moderate coronary atherosclerotic calcifications are stable.
There is no pericardial effusion.  Limited views of the abdominal viscera
appear within normal limits.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:  No bone destructive lesion or acute fracture is
identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Recurrent, severe, multifocal consolidation on a background of chronic
infiltrative pulmonary disease is likely related to either acute alveolitis or
hemorrhage due to recent crack cocaine inhalation.  Other possibilities
include cocaine-induced eosinophilic lung disease, which could be diagnosed
via BAL or peripheral blood smear.  There may be a component of pulmonary
edema, and concurrent pneumonia would be difficult to recognize. Chro

2.  13-mm right upper lobe pulmonary nodule at least four months old should be
monitored.

3.  Moderate biventricular cardiomegaly responsible for small, but increased
pleural effusions.

4.  Bulky mediastinal lymphadenopathy could be due to chronic, recurrent
pulmonary condition. HIV related adenopathy is another possibility.

5.  No pulmonary embolism or acute aortic syndrome.
